I've added a rule to the spec that every panel header gets a 1px bottom border matching its panel's body colour; the code isn't changed yet. `piton check` finds no problems, formatting is clean, and `piton build` succeeded.

**What I changed:**
- **The general rule** is in `SidebarShape.headers` in `spec/ui/components/sidebar/index.pi`:
  - Every panel header, in a sidebar or anywhere else a panel has one, has a 1px border along its bottom, inside the header's own height.
  - The border is exactly the colour of the body of the panel it heads.
  - It shows at every display scale and in light and dark mode, and it follows the body's colour when that changes, for example with the brightness slider.
- **Panel keyword** (`spec/ui/components/sidebar/Panel.pi`): the header sentence every panel inherits now mentions the border.
- **`RightSidebarShape.look`** (`spec/ui/components/right-sidebar/index.pi`) and **`GitPanelShape.look`** (`spec/ui/components/git-panel/index.pi`): both point to the rule. The Git panel's is #222222 in dark mode, and the Git panel now imports `SidebarScope` to link to it.

**Anchors the code should follow:**
- **`SidebarShape.headers`**, plus the panel sentence in **`Panel`**, **`RightSidebarShape.look`** and **`GitPanelShape.look`**.
- **In the code, there are two places that draw panel headers:**
  - `crate::sidebar::header` in `src/sidebar.rs`, used by the right sidebar's panels and the file tree. It needs a bottom border in the body colour of the panel it's used in; for the right sidebar that's `palette.ribbon`. It may need a parameter, since panel bodies differ.
  - `render` in `src/git_panel.rs`, which builds its own header row (`git-header`). It needs `.border_b_1()` in `palette.ribbon`.

  In both, the border should sit inside the existing 32px height, so layouts and tests that measure header height stay the same.

content.text:
Panel headers now have a 1px bottom border in their panel body's colour. That applies to the right sidebar's three panel headers and the Git panel's header. The border sits inside the existing 32px height, so nothing moves. It builds without warnings and pixel tests confirm the colours, but I haven't looked at it in the app.

- **Right sidebar** (Referenced Spec, Understanding, Subagents): the shared `header` helper in `src/sidebar.rs` now takes the body colour as a parameter. `src/referenced_spec.rs` passes the sidebar's body colour, #222222 in dark mode.
- **Git panel:** its header row in `src/git_panel.rs` has the same border in its body colour, also #222222 in dark mode.

The spec step said the file tree uses the shared header too, but it doesn't in the code: the only callers are the three right-sidebar panels. So those and the Git panel are the only panel headers that exist now.

**Tests:** two tests assumed the header's colour runs to its very last pixel, so I updated them:
- **Git panel look test:** now checks the header's last pixel row is the body colour, with the header colour above it.
- **Right sidebar look test:** same pixel check for each header. It also asserted there's no border anywhere in the sidebar, so it now allows this one body-coloured bottom border.

Both pass, as do all 17 Git panel tests. `referenced_spec_shows_the_understanding` failed once in one run, then passed three times in a row on its own. It tests double-click reset, which this change doesn't touch.

The full suite has 6 failures:
- Four were failing before this work: the three prompt-wording tests and `code_tasks_sent_to_spec_are_told_what_the_code_task_did`.
- `batch_sent_tasks_run_in_order_in_the_other_mode` and `raw_prompt_opens_once_the_task_has_compiled` have passed on their own in earlier runs; I didn't rerun them this time.

The spec and your prompt agree. The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1790715329-Prompt_daf9cb1c7859001f.understanding.md`.
